findings.title: source and partitive access
findings.claim: مِنْ makes Joseph's settling draw from portions of the definite land rather than naming a detached residence.
findings.mechanism: The source/partitive particle points back through the suffixal phrase to ٱلْأَرْضِ and is followed by حَيْثُ, linking movement to available portions before the place-scope opens.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees settlement as movement through the land's parts, not merely static occupancy.
findings.containment: This keeps the ordinary source and partitive grammar in view; it does not assert unlimited jurisdiction or a separate root sense.

epistemic.reason: The claim is directly tied to supplied focus wording, morphology, and trusted word-analysis support.

findings.title: qiraat ending as grammatical pressure
findings.claim: The supplied ending variation on حَيْثُ preserves its locative wherever function while exposing a grammatical difference at the clause boundary.
findings.mechanism: The variant readings alter final-vowel analysis at the same adverbial position, while both keep the place expression attached to the will clause.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted recitational variation can mark grammatical pressure without changing the phrase's open-place work.
findings.containment: Only the ending and its grammatical coloring are retained here; the wherever function remains live, and no extra agency conclusion is imported from the variant.

epistemic.reason: The focus alignment is accepted and the source supplies a bounded variant, formula, or echo; the finding keeps its stated restriction visible.

findings.title: wherever-will freedom formula
findings.claim: حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ forms an open wherever-plus-will expression: the place remains open until willing selects it.
findings.mechanism: The locative adverb supplies unbounded place-scope, while the following will verb supplies the selecting action within the land opened by مِنْهَا.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the granted freedom as a range of possible places rather than a single named station.
findings.containment: This is a local formulaic pressure carried by the supplied words; it does not import the external parallels as additional context or claim that every possible place is meant.

epistemic.reason: The claim is directly tied to supplied focus wording, morphology, and trusted word-analysis support.

findings.title: open locative scope
findings.claim: حَيْثُ opens the scope of Joseph's settling to wherever the will clause selects within the land.
findings.mechanism: The indeclinable locative is completed by يَشَاءُ, so the clause names a place-range rather than a fixed station; مِنْهَا keeps that range inside the land.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices spatial freedom as a grammatical effect of the place expression.
findings.containment: The scope is broad within the stated land-domain; it does not become unlimited world-wide rule.

epistemic.reason: The claim is directly tied to supplied focus wording, morphology, and trusted word-analysis support.

findings.title: Joseph’s delegated will
findings.claim: In the standard alignment, يَشَاءُ keeps Joseph as the agent who chooses where to settle within the granted land.
findings.mechanism: The third-person masculine imperfect agrees with the ongoing settlement subject and governs the locative scope after the completed divine establishment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that Joseph's authority includes operational choice, not only a title or appointment.
findings.containment: The choice is delegated and domain-bound; this finding leaves the supplied variant agency reading live.

epistemic.reason: The claim is directly tied to supplied focus wording, morphology, and trusted word-analysis support.

findings.mechanism: The variant bears on the same حَيْثُ + شَاءَ sequence, so the agency attribution changes while the locative operation remains attached to settlement.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices a second way the clause can hold place-selection and divine agency together without losing the standard delegated-human reading.
findings.containment: Both agency possibilities are retained without a verdict; the variant does not erase the canonical local alignment or enlarge the clause beyond its place-selection role.

findings.containment: The ordinary reaching reading remains intact. The rain-like arrival is a local image, not literal weather, and the incompatible imported root distribution is not activated.
